definition: The configuration values set before training — learning rate, batch size, architecture choices — that are not learned from data but shape how learning proceeds.
details: The configuration values set before training — learning rate, batch size, architecture choices — that are not learned from data but shape how learning proceeds.

explainer.lead: Machine learning hyperparameters are configuration values set before training — learning rate, batch size, architecture choices — that are not learned from data. They matter because they shape how learning proceeds.

tiers.eli5: They are the dials you set before the machine starts studying, and the settings change how well it learns.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose hyperparameters before training and tune them, since training does not set them from data. The pitfall is treating them as learned parameters.
tiers.paperLevel: Configuration values fixed before training — learning rate, batch size, architecture choices — that are not learned from data but shape how learning proceeds. The given facts state no selection procedure or limits.

explainer.example: Before training starts, the learning rate and batch size are chosen; training then proceeds under those settings without learning them from data.
